tier2.text: INVENTED FIXTURE - The premium end of this device market is an effective duopoly: the filer holds 55 percent of units above the 800 dollar price point and Peer Devices Inc holds 31 percent. The filer wins on the software its own devices run, which 92 percent of its customers keep when they replace a handset. A customer who buys nothing keeps a working device for about 4 years, and the replacement cycle is what every quarter's unit figure is priced against.

AAPL.what_it_does: INVENTED FIXTURE - The company designs and sells premium consumer computing devices, and sells subscriptions and a payments service to the people who own them. Its customers are households and, increasingly, corporate fleets. If it vanished, a customer would lose the device and the software that carries their photographs, messages and payment credentials, and would have to move all of it to a rival system that does not read the same file formats.

what_is_changing.statement: INVENTED FIXTURE - Services grew from 25000 to 27900 million dollars while devices grew from 60000 to 62100. Services carry a higher margin and recur monthly, so the mix shift lifts the blended margin even when device units are flat. The question is whether services can keep growing at that rate on a device base that is no longer expanding.

decisive_metrics.name: Services revenue against last year
decisive_metrics.why_it_decides: Services is the recurring, higher-margin half. Its growth rate is what carries the rating this question asks about.

decisive_metrics.name: Gross margin guided against delivered
decisive_metrics.why_it_decides: The mix shift is only real if it shows in the margin management guides to and then delivers.

decisive_metrics.name: Cash returned against cash generated
decisive_metrics.why_it_decides: Most of this company's return to an owner arrives as buybacks. Whether the cash covers them decides whether they continue.

decisive_metrics.name: Revenue from Greater China
decisive_metrics.why_it_decides: The single largest concentration of demand risk, and the line that moves the whole rating when it turns.

decisive_metrics.name: Price/earnings, against its own history and peers
decisive_metrics.why_it_decides: The business is rated on earnings against its own history and its peers, and this multiple is the number that rating divides the market value by.
